case.title: The Storage Room Murder
case.motive_summary: {VICTIM_NAME} betrayed {KILLER_NAME} regarding a vital partnership agreement.
case.overview_text: 08:12 — {VICTIM_NAME}, owner of Hobbs Cafe, found dead in the cafe storage room by {RH2_NAME}. The cafe opened at 08:00. Several villagers passed nearby between 07:30 and 08:10. No one claims to have seen what happened. The morning can be rewound from 06:00.

agents.routine_summary: Up at six, reviews the books in {VICTIM_DET} study, at the cafe by a quarter to seven to oversee opening.
agents.voice_card: Speaks in ledgers and verdicts; every sentence sounds like a final decision.

agents.routine_summary: Lives above the cafe. Down by half six to prep, opens the doors at eight sharp.
agents.voice_card: Precise and clipped; clips sentences even shorter when defensive, and never volunteers more than was asked.

agents.routine_summary: Morning delivery round through the square and rear alley; usually cadges a coffee when the cafe opens.
agents.voice_card: Rambles cheerfully, over-explains when nervous, and tends to answer a question you didn't ask.

agents.routine_summary: Opens the bookshop at nine; mornings are for paperwork and coffee at Hobbs.
agents.voice_card: Measured, almost rehearsed; pauses before answering and chooses polite words with visible care.

agents.routine_summary: In the timber yard from early; takes deliveries around half seven.
agents.voice_card: Blunt, short sentences, no hedging; gets louder rather than more careful when pressed.

agents.routine_summary: Opens up the bookshop stockroom early, then shelves new deliveries.
agents.voice_card: Soft-spoken and apologetic; qualifies everything ('I think', 'maybe') and trails off under pressure.

agents.routine_summary: Early shift at the clinic; crosses the square a few times each morning.
agents.voice_card: Calm, clinical phrasing; states observations like chart notes and avoids speculation.

agents.routine_summary: First on the square bench every morning with a flask and opinions.
agents.voice_card: Talks like a teacher mid-lesson; fond of rhetorical questions and certain of every detail.

locations.name: Village Square
locations.description: The open heart of the village, with a stone fountain, benches, and a view of the cafe and bookshop fronts.

locations.name: Hobbs Cafe
locations.description: The village cafe. Counter, tables, and the till at the front; kitchen behind.

locations.name: Cafe Kitchen
locations.description: The working kitchen behind the cafe counter. Coat hooks, sink, mop bucket in the corner.

locations.name: Cafe Storage Room
locations.description: A cramped storage room behind the kitchen, stacked with crates. A rear door opens onto the alley.

locations.name: Rear Alley
locations.description: A narrow service alley running behind the cafe and bookshop. Bins, crates, and the cafe's rear door.

locations.name: Reed & Bell Bookshop
locations.description: {RH2_NAME}'s bookshop, part-funded by {VICTIM_NAME}. Its back door opens onto the rear alley.

locations.name: Village Clinic
locations.description: A small clinic on the square where {WITNESS2_NAME} Cole works the early shift.

locations.name: {VICTIM_NAME}'s House
locations.description: {VICTIM_NAME}'s house on the edge of the square. {VICTIM_DET_CAP} study holds the cafe's books.

locations.name: {RH1_NAME}'s House & Yard
locations.description: {RH1_NAME}'s house and builder's timber yard on the far side of the square.

locations.name: Flat above Hobbs Cafe
locations.description: {KILLER_NAME}'s small flat above the cafe, reached by a side stair.

locations.name: Fountain
locations.description: The stone fountain in the middle of the village square.

objects.name: Brass {WEAPON_NAME}
objects.description: A heavy brass weight normally kept beside the till to pin down receipts.

objects.name: Torn ledger page
objects.description: A page torn from the cafe ledger, columns of till takings with discrepancies circled in red ink.

objects.name: Blue wool coat
objects.description: {KILLER_NAME}'s blue coat, well known around the village.

objects.name: {VICTIM_NAME}'s loan book
objects.description: A private notebook in {VICTIM_NAME}'s study recording money he is owed.

objects.name: Partnership letter
objects.description: A signed letter in {VICTIM_NAME}'s coat pocket naming {WITNESS4_NAME} — not {RH2_NAME} — as partner in the bookshop expansion.

objects.name: {RH2_NAME}'s handwritten note
objects.description: A folded note in {VICTIM_NAME}'s pocket: 'We settle this at 8. Don't make me ask twice. — I.R.'

memories.summary: {KILLER_NAME} has been skimming cash from the cafe till for over a year to cover {KILLER_DET} late mother's care debts.
Last week {VICTIM_NAME} showed {KILLER_NAME} the torn ledger page proving the theft and said: 'You have until tomorrow.' The deadline was this morning.
At 07:40 {VICTIM_NAME} told {KILLER_NAME} to meet {VICTIM_OBJ} in the storage room before opening — 'last chance to say it in your own words.'
{KILLER_NAME}'s prepared story: {KILLER_SUBJ} stepped out to the fountain for air from about 07:45 to just before 08:00, then opened the cafe.
{KILLER_NAME} washed the {WEAPON_NAME} and pushed it into the mop bucket at 08:02. {KILLER_SUBJ_CAP} is terrified someone will look in the kitchen.
{VICTIM_NAME} found the till discrepancies while doing the quarterly books and tore out the page as proof.
{VICTIM_NAME} planned to confront {KILLER_NAME} before opening and, if {KILLER_SUBJ} refused to confess, take the ledger page to the village committee at nine.
{VICTIM_NAME} signed the bookshop expansion over to {WITNESS4_NAME}, breaking {VICTIM_DET} promise to {RH2_NAME}. {VICTIM_SUBJ_CAP} planned to tell {RH2_NAME} at their 8 o'clock meeting.
{RH1_NAME} owes {VICTIM_NAME} £8,000, due today. {VICTIM_NAME} told {RH1_OBJ} last night {VICTIM_SUBJ} would raise it at the village committee if unpaid.
{RH2_NAME} heard a rumour the partnership went to {WITNESS4_NAME}. {RH2_SUBJ_CAP} wrote {VICTIM_NAME} a furious note demanding they settle it at 8 this morning.
{RH2_NAME} arrived at 08:05 for the meeting, waited, then found {VICTIM_NAME} dead in the storage room at 08:12 when {KILLER_NAME} said {VICTIM_SUBJ} must be out the back.
{RH2_NAME} was at the clinic with {WITNESS2_NAME} from 07:40 to 08:00 having {RH2_DET} blood pressure checked — {RH2_SUBJ} nearly cancelled the {VICTIM_NAME} meeting over the stress.
{RH1_NAME} owes {VICTIM_NAME} £8,000 {RH1_SUBJ} cannot repay. Being named at the committee would finish {RH1_DET} business.
{RH1_NAME} confronted {VICTIM_NAME} outside the cafe at 07:05 and it turned into a shouting match about the money.
{RH1_NAME} was back in {RH1_DET} yard from 07:15 signing for a timber delivery; the driver was with {RH1_OBJ} until 08:05.
{WITNESS1_NAME} saw someone in a blue coat slip into the rear alley at about 07:47. {WITNESS1_SUBJ_CAP} didn't see the face but assumes it was {KILLER_NAME} — {KILLER_SUBJ} always wears that coat.
{WITNESS1_NAME} was in the alley at 07:45 to meet {WITNESS4_NAME} — they've been seeing each other in secret because {RH2_NAME} disapproves of workplace romance.
While in the alley {WITNESS1_NAME} heard a dull thud from inside the cafe's back rooms just before {WITNESS1_SUBJ} and {WITNESS4_NAME} left, around 07:56.
{WITNESS4_NAME} knows {VICTIM_NAME} chose {WITNESS4_OBJ} for the partnership and that {RH2_NAME} doesn't officially know yet. {WITNESS4_SUBJ_CAP}'s been dreading the fallout.
{WITNESS4_NAME} met {WITNESS1_NAME} behind the bookshop at 07:45. {WITNESS4_SUBJ_CAP} will not admit it unless confronted — {RH2_NAME} would make {WITNESS4_DET} life miserable.
Passing the cafe window at 07:40, {WITNESS2_NAME} heard {VICTIM_NAME} say something like 'storage room, before we open' — {WITNESS2_SUBJ} couldn't hear who {VICTIM_SUBJ} was talking to.
{WITNESS2_NAME} took {RH2_NAME}'s blood pressure at the clinic from about 07:40 to 08:00. {RH2_NAME} was agitated about a meeting.
Last week {WITNESS3_NAME} was in the cafe when {WITNESS3_SUBJ} heard {VICTIM_NAME}, low and furious, tell someone in the kitchen doorway: 'You have until tomorrow.' {WITNESS3_SUBJ_CAP} never saw who.

{WITNESS3_NAME} is convinced {RH1_NAME} must be the killer — 'you should have heard {RH1_OBJ} this morning, practically frothing.' {WITNESS3_SUBJ_CAP} connects the argument to the murder with no evidence.
Village rumour: {VICTIM_NAME} was planning to 'shake up' the bookshop arrangement. Nobody knows details, but {RH2_NAME} heard it too.

events.truth_description: {VICTIM_NAME} rises early and takes {VICTIM_DET} coffee into the study.
{VICTIM_NAME} works through the cafe ledger in {VICTIM_DET} study and slips a torn page into {VICTIM_DET} coat pocket.
events.player_description: A light is on in {VICTIM_NAME}'s study.

events.truth_description: {KILLER_NAME} comes down from {KILLER_DET} flat and starts prepping the cafe: chairs down, machine on, float counted.
{WITNESS3_NAME} takes {WITNESS3_DET} usual bench in the square with a flask of tea, facing the cafe.
{VICTIM_NAME} arrives at the cafe. {VICTIM_SUBJ_CAP} and {KILLER_NAME} exchange a few stiff words; the room goes quiet when {VICTIM_SUBJ} checks the till.
{WITNESS2_NAME} opens up the clinic for the early shift.
{WITNESS4_NAME} lets {WITNESS4_REFL} into the bookshop to sort the morning delivery in the stockroom.
{RH1_NAME} confronts {VICTIM_NAME} outside the cafe. Voices rise fast — money, a deadline, the committee. {RH1_NAME} jabs a finger at {VICTIM_NAME}'s chest before storming off.
{RH1_NAME} returns to {RH1_DET} yard, still fuming, and starts hauling timber about.
{RH2_NAME} strides into the cafe, presses a folded note into {VICTIM_NAME}'s hand without a word, and leaves.
events.player_description: {RH2_NAME} enters the cafe briefly and hands {VICTIM_NAME} something small, then leaves without ordering.

events.truth_description: {WITNESS1_NAME} parks {WITNESS1_DET} van by the square and starts {WITNESS1_DET} delivery round, crates stacked on a trolley.
{KILLER_NAME} tidies the counter, moving the {WEAPON_NAME} onto the receipt pile.
{VICTIM_NAME} tells {KILLER_NAME}, quietly: 'Storage room, before we open. Last chance to say it in your own words.'
events.player_description: {VICTIM_NAME} speaks to {KILLER_NAME} in a low voice near the kitchen door. A phrase drifts through the open window: '...storage room, before we open...'

events.truth_description: {RH2_NAME} arrives at the clinic, tense and pale, and asks {WITNESS2_NAME} to check {RH2_DET} blood pressure before 'a difficult meeting'.
{KILLER_NAME} takes {KILLER_DET} blue coat and slips out of the cafe's front door, turning towards the square.
{WITNESS1_NAME} and {WITNESS4_NAME} meet behind the bookshop's back door, out of sight, talking in whispers.
events.player_description: Two figures stand close together at the bookshop end of the alley, mostly hidden by the bins.

events.truth_description: {KILLER_NAME}, in {KILLER_DET} blue coat, cuts from the square into the rear alley and stops by the cafe's rear door.
events.player_description: A figure in a blue coat enters the rear alley from the square and moves towards the cafe's rear door.

events.truth_description: {VICTIM_NAME} walks through the kitchen into the storage room carrying {VICTIM_DET} coat, the ledger page in the pocket.
events.player_description: {VICTIM_NAME} is no longer visible in the cafe front.

events.truth_description: {KILLER_NAME} enters the storage room through the rear door, the {WEAPON_NAME} in {KILLER_DET} coat pocket.
The confrontation turns. {VICTIM_NAME} says the committee will hear everything at nine. {KILLER_NAME} strikes {VICTIM_OBJ} with the {WEAPON_NAME}.
The blow is audible in the alley as a dull thud.
events.player_description: A dull thud is heard from inside the cafe's back rooms.

events.truth_description: {KILLER_NAME} slips out of the rear door, pulls it shut, and walks quickly up the alley towards the square, one hand pressed into {KILLER_DET} coat pocket.
events.player_description: The cafe's rear door opens briefly. A figure leaves carrying something small and walks quickly towards the square.

events.truth_description: {WITNESS1_NAME} and {WITNESS4_NAME} separate hurriedly — {WITNESS4_NAME} back through the bookshop's rear door, {WITNESS1_NAME} around to {WITNESS1_DET} van.
events.player_description: The two figures at the bookshop end of the alley separate and leave in different directions.

events.truth_description: {KILLER_NAME} re-enters through the front, hangs {KILLER_DET} coat in the kitchen, and unlocks the cafe doors two minutes late, visibly flushed.
events.player_description: {KILLER_NAME} opens the cafe doors, slightly late, looking flustered.

events.truth_description: {KILLER_NAME} rinses the {WEAPON_NAME} at the kitchen sink and pushes it down into the mop bucket.
{WITNESS3_NAME} comes in for {WITNESS3_DET} usual coffee. {KILLER_NAME} fumbles {WITNESS3_DET} change; {WITNESS3_SUBJ} remarks that {KILLER_SUBJ} looks like {KILLER_SUBJ}'s seen a ghost.
{RH2_NAME} arrives for {RH2_DET} 8 o'clock meeting with {VICTIM_NAME} and takes a table, drumming {RH2_DET} fingers.
{RH2_NAME} demands to know where {VICTIM_NAME} is. {KILLER_NAME}, not meeting {RH2_DET} eyes, says {VICTIM_SUBJ}'s probably out the back.
{RH2_NAME} pushes through the kitchen into the storage room and finds {VICTIM_NAME} dead on the floor. {RH2_DET_CAP} scream empties the square.
events.player_description: {RH2_NAME} finds {VICTIM_NAME} dead in the storage room. {RH2_DET_CAP} scream is heard across the square.

clues.title: Torn ledger page on the body
clues.description: In {VICTIM_NAME}'s coat pocket: a page torn from the cafe ledger. Till takings for the past year, with shortfalls circled in red and a note in {VICTIM_NAME}'s hand — 'C. — until tomorrow.'

clues.title: "You have until tomorrow"
clues.description: {WITNESS3_NAME} heard {VICTIM_NAME}, low and furious, tell someone in the cafe kitchen doorway last week: 'You have until tomorrow.' {WITNESS3_SUBJ_CAP} never saw who it was.

clues.title: Audited ledger with missing page
clues.description: The cafe ledger in {VICTIM_NAME}'s study is covered in fresh audit marks. One page has been torn out — the stub remains. Someone at the cafe was stealing, and {VICTIM_NAME} knew.

clues.title: Blue coat in the rear alley
clues.description: {WITNESS1_NAME} saw someone in a blue coat slip into the rear alley at about 07:47 and head for the cafe's rear door. {WITNESS1_SUBJ_CAP} didn't see the face, but {KILLER_NAME} always wears that blue coat.

clues.title: Dull thud at 07:56
clues.description: A dull thud was heard from the cafe's back rooms at 07:56 — inside the murder window, in the room where the body was found.

clues.title: Figure leaving by the rear door at 07:58
clues.description: The cafe's rear door opened briefly at 07:58. A figure left carrying something small and walked quickly towards the square.

clues.title: The {WEAPON_NAME} is gone
clues.description: The {WEAPON_NAME} sat on the counter at 07:36 — {KILLER_NAME} moved it {KILLER_REFL}. After the body was found, it is nowhere on the counter.

clues.title: Till weight in the mop bucket
clues.description: The {WEAPON_NAME}, found pushed down inside the kitchen mop bucket. It has been rinsed but is still damp — and it doesn't belong anywhere near the sink.

clues.title: Damp sleeve on {KILLER_NAME}'s coat
clues.description: {KILLER_NAME}'s blue coat hangs in the kitchen. The right sleeve is damp at the cuff and faintly smudged, as if something wet was carried against it.

clues.title: "Storage room, before we open"
clues.description: Passing the cafe window at 07:40, {WITNESS2_NAME} heard {VICTIM_NAME} say 'storage room, before we open'. {WITNESS2_SUBJ_CAP} couldn't hear who {VICTIM_SUBJ} was speaking to — but whoever it was knew where {VICTIM_NAME} would be.

clues.title: {RH1_NAME}'s shouting match with {VICTIM_NAME}
clues.description: At 07:05 {RH1_NAME} confronted {VICTIM_NAME} outside the cafe — money, a deadline, the committee. {RH1_SUBJ_CAP} jabbed a finger in {VICTIM_NAME}'s chest and stormed off. Half the square heard it.

clues.title: {VICTIM_NAME}'s loan book
clues.description: A private notebook in {VICTIM_NAME}'s study: 'O. Price — £8,000 — due 1st. Committee if unpaid.' {RH1_NAME} had everything to lose today.

clues.title: {RH1_NAME}'s timber delivery
clues.description: {RH1_NAME} was in {RH1_DET} yard from 07:15 signing for a timber delivery. The driver was with {RH1_OBJ} until after eight — right through the murder window.

clues.title: {RH2_NAME}'s note on the body
clues.description: A folded note in {VICTIM_NAME}'s pocket: 'We settle this at 8. Don't make me ask twice. — I.R.' {RH2_NAME} wanted something from {VICTIM_NAME}, badly, this morning.

clues.title: The partnership letter
clues.description: A signed letter in {VICTIM_NAME}'s coat: the bookshop expansion goes to {WITNESS4_NAME} — not {RH2_NAME}. {VICTIM_NAME} broke {VICTIM_DET} promise, and today {VICTIM_SUBJ} was going to say so to {RH2_NAME}'s face.

clues.title: {RH2_NAME}'s clinic visit
clues.description: {WITNESS2_NAME} took {RH2_NAME}'s blood pressure at the clinic from about 07:40 to 08:00 — covering the whole murder window. {RH2_NAME} was agitated about 'a difficult meeting'.

clues.title: Nobody at the fountain
clues.description: {WITNESS3_NAME} sat facing the fountain from 06:40 onwards and does not recall seeing {KILLER_NAME} there between 07:45 and 08:00 — though {WITNESS3_SUBJ} admits {WITNESS3_SUBJ} had {WITNESS3_DET} crossword.

clues.title: {WITNESS1_NAME} and {WITNESS4_NAME}'s secret meeting
clues.description: {WITNESS1_NAME} was in the alley at 07:45 to meet {WITNESS4_NAME} — they've been seeing each other in secret. That's why {WITNESS1_SUBJ} was there, and why neither of them wanted to say so.

conclusions.summary: {KILLER_NAME} was stealing from the till; {VICTIM_NAME} had proof and a deadline of this morning.
{KILLER_NAME} was at the cafe's rear door during the murder window, despite claiming to be at the fountain.
{KILLER_NAME} had the {WEAPON_NAME} — {KILLER_SUBJ} handled it at 07:36, it vanished in the murder window, and it was found rinsed in the kitchen {KILLER_SUBJ} controls.
{VICTIM_NAME} was struck with the {WEAPON_NAME} in the storage room at about 07:56.
{KILLER_NAME}'s fountain alibi is false — {KILLER_SUBJ} was seen entering the rear alley at 07:47, a figure left the rear door at 07:58, and nobody saw {KILLER_DET} at the fountain.
{RH1_NAME} had a desperate financial motive and argued publicly with {VICTIM_NAME} an hour before the murder.
{RH1_NAME} was with the timber delivery driver through the entire murder window.
{RH2_NAME} was betrayed over the partnership and demanded a showdown with {VICTIM_NAME} this very morning.
{RH2_NAME} was at the clinic with {WITNESS2_NAME} from 07:40 to 08:00.
{WITNESS1_NAME} was lurking in the rear alley during the murder window and is evasive about why.
{WITNESS1_NAME} was in the alley to meet {WITNESS4_NAME} in secret — nothing to do with {VICTIM_NAME}.

default_answers.alibi: I told you — I stepped out for some air before opening. It was a normal morning until {RH2_NAME} screamed.
default_answers.timeline: Prepping the cafe, mostly. Chairs, coffee machine, the float. The same as every morning.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: He was here first thing. After that I was busy with the counter.
default_answers.relationship: He owned the cafe. I run it. We kept things professional.
default_answers.evidence: I don't know anything about that.
default_answers.location: I don't spend much time thinking about that place, to be honest.

rules.answer_text: How we met? I answered a card in his window fifteen years ago — waitress, five mornings a week. He watched me cash up my first till and then recounted it in front of everyone. I stayed anyway. You don't forget who gave you your start — or who never let you forget it, either.
He was exacting. Checked everything twice, trusted no one to do it right. But he gave me the manager's job when nobody else would, so we made it work.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} describes {KILLER_DET} relationship with {VICTIM_NAME} as strict but workable, and says {VICTIM_SUBJ} 'trusted no one'.

suggested_followups: How did you two first meet?

rules.answer_text: I was at the fountain from about a quarter to eight until just before opening. I needed air — {VICTIM_NAME} had been on edge all morning and it gets to you. Then I opened up at eight.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} claims {KILLER_SUBJ} was at the fountain from about 07:45 until just before 08:00.

suggested_followups: Who saw you at the fountain?
Why did you need air?

rules.answer_text: That's when I was out at the fountain. I stepped out around a quarter to and came back to open the doors. Ask {WITNESS3_NAME} — {WITNESS3_SUBJ}'s always on that bench.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} claims {KILLER_SUBJ} was at the fountain from about 07:45 until just before 08:00.

suggested_followups: Did {WITNESS3_NAME} actually see you there?

rules.answer_text: Down at half six, prep until {VICTIM_NAME} arrived at a quarter to seven. {VICTIM_SUBJ_CAP} checked the till — {VICTIM_SUBJ}'d been doing that a lot lately. {RH1_NAME} turned up around seven and made a scene outside. After that, more prep.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} says {KILLER_SUBJ} was prepping the cafe from 06:30 and that {VICTIM_NAME} had been checking the till often lately.

rules.answer_text: About twenty to eight, I suppose. He said he had things to sort in the back before we opened. I didn't see him again. I wish I'd... checked on him.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} claims {KILLER_SUBJ} last saw {VICTIM_NAME} around 07:40 when {VICTIM_SUBJ} went to the back, and never saw {VICTIM_OBJ} again.

suggested_followups: What did he need to sort in the back?

rules.answer_text: The {WEAPON_NAME}? It lives on the counter. If it's not there, someone's moved it — people fiddle with it all the time. {WITNESS1_NAME} plays with it while {WITNESS1_SUBJ} waits for {WITNESS1_DET} coffee.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} claims {KILLER_SUBJ} doesn't know where the {WEAPON_NAME} is and suggests others handle it often.

rules.answer_text: I keep the till. {VICTIM_NAME} kept the books. If there were mistakes in those columns they were {VICTIM_DET} sums, not mine. 'C' could be anyone — customer, carried-over, anything.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} denies the ledger discrepancies have anything to do with {KILLER_OBJ}.

rules.answer_text: The alley? I had no reason to be back there. Deliveries come in the morning through the front until we open the rear for the bins. I was at the fountain, as I said.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} denies being in the rear alley this morning.

rules.answer_text: I hadn't been in the storage room since yesterday's stocktake. {VICTIM_NAME} dealt with the back {VICTIM_REFL} these days. {VICTIM_SUBJ_CAP}'d... changed the lock rota, actually. Didn't say why.

claims.summary: {KILLER_NAME} claims {KILLER_SUBJ} had not been in the storage room since yesterday.

default_answers.alibi: Doing my round, mate. Van by the square, crates in and out. Same as every day.
default_answers.timeline: On my round somewhere. It all blurs together a bit, honestly.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Properly spoke to him? Day before yesterday, when I dropped the coffee order.
default_answers.relationship: {VICTIM_NAME} was alright. Paid on time, tipped at Christmas. No trouble between us.
default_answers.evidence: Couldn't tell you anything about that.
default_answers.location: I'm all over the village in a morning, take your pick.

rules.answer_text: First met him on my first delivery round, must be six years back now. He signed for the flour, then told me I'd stacked it wrong and showed me exactly how he wanted it. Every week since — same time, same nod. You get to know a man by his routines.

No quarrel with {VICTIM_NAME}, none. {VICTIM_SUBJ_CAP} had {VICTIM_DET} moods lately, mind — snapping at {KILLER_NAME}, double-counting the till like it owed {VICTIM_OBJ} money. Something was eating {VICTIM_OBJ}.

claims.summary: {WITNESS1_NAME} says {VICTIM_NAME} had been in a foul mood lately, snapping at {KILLER_NAME} and repeatedly counting the till.

suggested_followups: How did you two first meet?

rules.answer_text: I was around the square and the back lane doing deliveries. Look, I was near the alley for a bit, alright? Just... sorting crates. Then I heard the scream same as everyone.

claims.summary: {WITNESS1_NAME} admits being near the rear alley during the murder window but says {WITNESS1_SUBJ} was 'sorting crates'.

suggested_followups: What were you really doing in the alley?
What did you see from there?

rules.answer_text: Right, so — I was down the alley end around then. Saw someone in a blue coat come in from the square about a quarter to... no, closer to ten-to. Went towards the cafe's back door. Didn't see the face but — that's {KILLER_NAME}'s coat, everyone knows it. And later there was this thud from inside. Dull, like a sack of flour going over. I didn't think anything of it. You don't, do you.

claims.summary: {WITNESS1_NAME} says {WITNESS1_SUBJ} saw someone in a blue coat — {WITNESS1_SUBJ} assumes {KILLER_NAME} — enter the alley at about 07:47 and head for the cafe's rear door.
{WITNESS1_NAME} says {WITNESS1_SUBJ} heard a dull thud from the cafe's back rooms while {WITNESS1_SUBJ} was in the alley, around 07:56.

suggested_followups: Why were you in the alley at that time?
Did the figure see you?

rules.answer_text: Crates. I told you. There's a stack behind the bookshop needs shifting most mornings. Why's everyone so interested in the alley all of a sudden?

claims.summary: {WITNESS1_NAME} admits being near the rear alley during the murder window but says {WITNESS1_SUBJ} was 'sorting crates'.

rules.answer_text: The brass thing? Yeah, it sits by the till. I flick it sometimes waiting for my coffee. It was there yesterday. Why, is it gone?

default_answers.alibi: I was at the clinic, then I came here for my meeting with {VICTIM_NAME}. You know the rest.
default_answers.timeline: Paperwork at the shop, then the clinic, then... the cafe.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Alive? At twenty past seven. I gave him a note about our meeting.
default_answers.relationship: We were business partners. He put money into my shop. It was... complicated lately.
default_answers.evidence: I can't help you with that.
default_answers.location: I know the village as well as anyone. What of it?

rules.answer_text: We met at the bank, of all places — both of us waiting on the same loan officer. He leaned over and said he'd finance the shop himself, at a fairer rate. It felt like a kindness at the time. It took me years to understand it was a leash.

epilogues.{KILLER_ID}: {KILLER_NAME} confessed the rest by evening, in the same flat voice {KILLER_SUBJ} had used all morning. {KILLER_SUBJ_CAP} asked, twice, whether anyone had told the village yet, and what they had said.
epilogues.{VICTIM_ID}: They shut {VICTIM_NAME}'s door for a fortnight and the village walked past it slower than usual. When it opened again under a new name, half of them went in out of guilt and stayed for the coffee.
epilogues.{RH1_ID}: {RH1_NAME} was a suspect for about two days and has dined out on it ever since. The telling gets longer every year, and the two days are now most of a week.
epilogues.{RH2_ID}: {RH2_NAME} was never charged with anything, and has still not entirely been forgiven — not for the murder, which {RH2_SUBJ} plainly did not do, but for everything the investigation turned up on the way past.
epilogues.{WITNESS1_ID}: {WITNESS1_NAME} gave the evidence that broke the case and has never once been thanked for it in public. {WITNESS1_SUBJ_CAP} says {WITNESS1_SUBJ} would rather not be, which is almost true.
epilogues.{WITNESS2_ID}: {WITNESS2_NAME} went back to work the following Monday, because the work was still there. It is astonishing, {WITNESS2_SUBJ} says, how much of grief is just turning up.
epilogues.{WITNESS3_ID}: {WITNESS3_NAME} tells the story to anyone who sits down long enough, and in {WITNESS3_DET} telling {WITNESS3_SUBJ} suspected the right person from the very first morning. Nobody corrects {WITNESS3_OBJ}.
